label: Genetic hitchhiking: a sweep's reduction of linked variation grows as c/s falls
statement_en: Under the deterministic-sweep approximation relHet = 1 - K^(-a c/s) with K > 1 and a > 0 (a named hypothesis), a selective sweep leaves no variation at a neutral site with c/s = 0, the variation left rises strictly with c/s (so the reduction is larger the tighter the linkage relative to selection), and for c/s > 0 the sweep removes some but not all variation.

hypotheses.name: Delphi.LeanBio.Hitchhiking.SweepHyp
hypotheses.statement: Relative heterozygosity after one sweep at a neutral site is relHet K a x = 1 - K^(-(a x)) with x = c/s (recombination fraction over selection coefficient), base K > 1 and rate a > 0. The exponential family is the shape of the deterministic-sweep approximation; whether it matches an equation of the 1974 paper exactly was not checked against the paper's text.
hypotheses.source: Maynard Smith J, Haigh J (1974) The hitch-hiking effect of a favourable gene. Genetical Research 23:23-35, doi:10.1017/S0016672300014634 (resolved via Crossref 2026-11-01); claim notation in math-bio-theorems/claims/key-claims.json

scope.basis: population-genetic model: one sweep of a new favourable mutation, two loci, deterministic allele-frequency trajectory, infinite-sites neutral locus. Not about background selection, which produces the same diversity-recombination correlation.

sources: claim-tests/math-bio-theorems/maynardsmith-hitchhiking/result.json (pre-registered; verdict supports: diversity correlates positively with recombination on human chr22, a pattern background selection also predicts)
